nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 午后的博卡普，薄荷绿、柠檬黄和珊瑚粉沿着石板路一路铺开。只有街角一面墙，灰得像忘记了自己的故事。

nodes.speaker: Amina
nodes.text: You came at the right time. This wall needs a new story, but the colour must come from the neighbourhood.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: Amina 递给你三张色卡，请你先去问问附近的居民，而不是替他们做决定。

options.text: 「What colour feels like home to you?」

nodes.speaker: 街坊奶奶
nodes.text: Home? Turquoise. It is the colour of the sea we can smell, even when we cannot see it.

nodes.speaker: 街坊奶奶
nodes.text: Blue is lovely, but ask me what it reminds me of. A good question leaves room for a story.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 你记下海的青绿、香料的金黄和傍晚天空的粉红。每种颜色后面，都跟着一个人的回忆。

nodes.speaker: Amina
nodes.text: Now tell me: what should people feel when they pass this wall?

options.text: 「They should feel invited to stop and talk.」
「They should feel proud of the stories here.」

nodes.speaker: Amina
nodes.text: Then we paint an open doorway. A mural can begin a conversation before anyone speaks.

nodes.speaker: Amina
nodes.text: Then every colour gets a name from the person who gave it to us. Pride should have signatures.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 太阳落到信号山背后时，灰墙已经变成一张巨大的社区明信片。路过的人不断停下，认出属于自己的那一种颜色。

nodes.speaker: Amina
nodes.text: Beautiful English is not about big words. It is about asking a question that lets someone be seen.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 【获得 120 金币】你留下了一枚手掌大小的色块，也带走了一个更好的提问方式。
